{{Article header|deck=Surface deposit mining removes targetable deposits from asteroids with an abrasion blaster.}}

'''Surface deposit mining''' is an asteroid-mining method that uses an [[Abrasion Blaster]] to break a visible, targetable deposit away from the rock for collection. The released fragment is collected manually through the cargo scoop or by a [[Collector Limpet Controller|collector limpet]], then processed by a [[Refinery]].<ref name="frontier-recap">[https://forums.frontier.co.uk/threads/content-recap-beyond-chapter-four-livestream-mining-and-squadrons.454587/ Content Recap: Beyond – Chapter Four Livestream – Mining and Squadrons], Frontier Developments, 1 November 2018.</ref><ref name="abrasion">[https://elite-dangerous.fandom.com/wiki/Abrasion_Blaster Abrasion Blaster], Elite Dangerous Wiki.</ref>

The method concerns deposits on '''asteroids'''. It is separate from [[Surface Mining]], which uses the Rhino and deployable mining rigs at Planetary Mining Locations.

== Mechanics ==

A surface deposit is a discrete feature attached to an asteroid rather than part of the ordinary mineral composition cut by a mining laser. When a prospector limpet scans a suitable asteroid, the cockpit display identifies its deposits and makes individual deposit targets available.<ref name="frontier-recap" />

A direct abrasion-blaster hit dislodges the selected deposit as a recoverable fragment. The blaster does not collect or refine that fragment, so the remaining cargo, limpet, and refinery parts of the mining loop still apply.

Surface deposits may be found on intact asteroids and on the exposed sections left after a core asteroid is split. They are therefore a mining method in their own right and also the normal extraction method for deposits exposed during [[Core Mining|core mining]].<ref name="mechanics">[https://edmining.com/elite-dangerous-mining-mechanics/ Elite Dangerous Mining Mechanics], ED Mining.</ref>

== Equipment relationships ==

* '''[[Abrasion Blaster]]:''' the required extraction tool. Its own article covers the module and available variants.
* '''[[Prospector Limpet Controller]]:''' identifies the asteroid's contents and marks deposit locations.
* '''[[Collector Limpet Controller]] or cargo scoop:''' recovers each dislodged fragment.
* '''[[Refinery]] and cargo space:''' process collected fragments and store finished commodities.
* '''[[Pulse Wave Analyser]]:''' helps locate asteroids with anomalous deposits. It is a search tool, not the extractor.

A ship configured for core mining usually carries the required abrasion blaster already because surface deposits remain after a successful detonation. A ship searching only for surface deposits does not need a seismic charge launcher unless it will also crack core asteroids.

== Relationship to other mining methods ==

* [[Laser Mining|Laser mining]] cuts ordinary fragments from the asteroid matrix with a mining laser.
* [[Sub-surface Mining|Sub-surface mining]] drills embedded deposits with a sub-surface displacement missile.
* Core mining places seismic charges in fissures to split a core asteroid.
* Surface deposit mining targets exposed deposits individually with an abrasion blaster.

An asteroid may support more than one method. The presence of a surface deposit does not mean its ordinary composition, sub-surface deposits, or core can be extracted with the abrasion blaster.

Commodity availability depends on the ring and the deposit generated on the asteroid. [[Mining Commodities]] compares known commodity sources without implying that every named mineral is available through every extraction method.

== Field Procedure ==

[[How to Mine Surface Deposits]] covers targeting, firing, collection, refinery checks, completion criteria, and common failures. The post-detonation sequence is also incorporated into [[How to Core Mine]].
